title: The IMAP extension was unbundled from php-src
summary: PHP 8.4 unbundled the IMAP extension from php-src and moved it to PECL, so a PHP 8.4+ build no longer ships `ext-imap` by default; it must be installed separately from PECL to keep using `imap_*` functions.
new_code_policy: Do not assume `ext-imap` is available on PHP 8.4+ just because it used to ship by default. Declare `ext-imap` explicitly in `composer.json` `require`, and for new work prefer a maintained userland IMAP client library (or a protocol-appropriate alternative) so the project does not depend on a PECL extension that must be separately compiled or packaged for every target environment.
existing_code_policy: Search for `imap_open()`, other `imap_*` calls and any `IMAP\Connection` type usage. Once the project's floor reaches PHP 8.4, confirm the deployment environment (containers, CI images, hosting provider) installs the PECL `imap` extension explicitly; a build that previously worked only because IMAP was bundled will fail with undefined-function errors otherwise. There is no code-level substitute: the functions are unchanged, only their packaging is, so no rewrite is needed once the extension is present.
guideline: Treat `ext-imap` as an optional, separately-installed PECL extension on PHP 8.4 and later, not as a bundled default. Declare it explicitly as a Composer platform requirement and verify it is installed wherever the application runs.
details: PHP 8.4's UPGRADING file lists the IMAP extension under '8. Removed Extensions and SAPIs': "The IMAP extension has been unbundled and moved to PECL" (RFC unbundle_imap_pspell_oci8). This is a packaging change, not a functional removal of the API: the `imap_*` functions themselves are not deleted, but a stock PHP 8.4+ build no longer compiles or ships the extension, so any code calling `imap_open()` or related functions will fail with undefined-function errors unless the PECL `imap` package is installed and enabled separately. No PHP 8.2, 8.3 or 8.5 UPGRADING file mentions IMAP, so there is no earlier deprecation notice and nothing further changes in 8.5; PHP 8.4 is the only lifecycle event on record.
notes: No automatic replacement is offered because this is a packaging/deployment change, not a mechanical code substitution: the fix is installing the PECL extension (or migrating to a userland IMAP client) in the target environment, which only a human reviewing the deployment can decide.

This is a removed-in-range case, not removed-across-range: under the tool's known PHP 8.2-8.5 minors, `imap` is still bundled on 8.2 and 8.3 and only unbundled starting at 8.4, so the affected minors are 8.4 and 8.5 while 8.2 and 8.3 remain unaffected.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.4.0.txt, '8. Removed Extensions and SAPIs' -> IMAP: "The IMAP extension has been unbundled and moved to PECL." Grepping the 8.2, 8.3 and 8.5 UPGRADING files for "IMAP" found no further mention.
